sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: 'Quality Checks' row 14 and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 14 (annotation: PII is defined in prompts by design; 'If task data itself contain credential flag it. Only in toml we allow.'); row 52 read for boundary
.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r1/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (Delivery profile, Known false positives: 'Flag real secrets or personal data in seed data')
evidence: Only shipped data file is environment/assets/kittle.json (5728 bytes); solution/app/seed/kittle.json is byte-identical (sha256 42ab8b97a160e0f739e50630502feadfafdeb78cea0979d7818d2e1f79646fc2 for both, matching raw-evidence-index.json entries). Scripted referential audit (python -I, json parse) found zero problems: 17 unique message ids K-1..K-17 with no gaps or duplicates; every parent (K-14->K-1, K-15->K-14, K-4->K-3, K-12->K-6, K-9->K-8) resolves inside the same matter and precedes its child, giving the 3-level chain K-1>K-14>K-15 the brief requires; messages are chronological per matter; all timestamps and version timestamps <= clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z; every author is a seeded account, clients author only in their own matter (gwen M-11/M-13, paul M-12), walled dev@ never authors in M-12; matter clients have role client and the wall lists only staff; every read_up_to entry references an account, a matter and a message in that matter, and no entry exists for a matter the account cannot see (dev has none for M-12, clients only for own matters). Accounts, roles and wall in kittle.json agree with walls-and-retention.md table and 'Dev Anand is walled from M-12'; timer_days values (7, null, 30) are within timer_options_days [null,1,7,30]. Timer boundaries are deliberate and consistent with the brief: on M-11 (7 days) K-1 (unheld, has reply K-14) and K-10 (sent exactly 7 days before the clock) expire at import, matching 'a message sent exactly seven days ago ... is already gone' and the placeholder rule; held K-2/K-17 survive; no read_up_to pointer targets an expiring message. Synthetic: names (Harriet Rowe, Dev Anand, Sian Lloyd, Gwen Pryce, Paul Marsh, Kittle & Rowe, Fenwick Mills) are generic fiction, emails use the reserved .test TLD, no phone/address/DOB/ID numbers. No credentials, tokens or keys appear in the seed (grep password/token/secret/api_key: none); the shared demo password lives only in walls-and-retention.md, which the profile and internal annotation allow. Injection: K-16 body is 'Pasted from the lease: Schedule 2 On hold [link](javascript:alert(2))'. This is an inert escaping fixture tied to a public requirement (conversations.md Formatting: markup 'is just text and shows exactly as it was typed ... Typing the words "On hold" ... mustn't make it look held') and graded by tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:167. It contains no prompt-injection or scoring directive, and every judge prompt treats submission content as untrusted (e.g. tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:4). Weak-app probe: an app that renders bodies with innerHTML executes onerror/alert and is caught by judge.toml:168 ('Fails if ... any dialog appears'), so the fixture helps discrimination rather than letting a broken app pass. Conforming-alternative probe: an app that sanitises (strips) the tags instead of escaping would fail, but the brief explicitly demands literal display, so that is a public requirement, not a seed defect. Why Note with risk=true rather than Pass: workbook row 14 literally says data must be 'free of ... injection payloads' and quality-checks.md:63 says 'free-text fields carry no injection payload'. The XSS string is, literally, such a payload. The intent (an escaping fixture backed by a public requirement) is defensible, but neither the workbook nor the skill has an exception for it. This conflict needs owner reconciliation and is not a confirmed defect; it carries hosted-QC flag risk (see the Colderwater lessons on literal portal flags). The seed fixture does not need runtime measurement for this row beyond the parse/reference audit above. The raw evidence index records scripted golden legs only, not a configured judge run.
counterexample: Not a demonstrated defect. Plausible hosted-QC reading: a reviewer applying row 14 literally cites kittle.json K-16 ' ... [link](javascript:alert(2))' as an injection payload in shipped seed data.
suggested_fix: Optional mitigation (owner decision): keep the escaping test but make the seed fixture non-executable, e.g. 'Schedule 2 On hold [link](ftp://lease)'. Adjust judge.toml:167 to match. Alternatively, record in the task rationale that K-16 is an intentional, inert escaping fixture required by conversations.md Formatting. Leave the judge-posted payload at judge.toml:164 to row 52.
